topic: User-defined Literal Suffixes for Complex Numbers
explanation: In modern C++, user-defined literal suffixes enable developers to create custom literal types and representations, allowing for more expressive and type-safe code. Specifically, for complex number literals, suffixes like 'i', 'il', and 'if' are used to construct complex numbers of specific types (e.g., complex<float>, complex<double>, complex<long double>) directly from literal values. This feature leverages operator overloading for user-defined literals, facilitating intuitive syntax for complex number initialization and enhancing code readability and correctness in numerical computations.
